program_plain: World: 400 self-propelled agents moving in a wrap-around 20x20 square. Rules each step: each agent takes the average heading of agents within distance 1, adds uniform heading noise spanning the full circle (2 pi rad), and moves at speed 0.3.
model_family: active matter / collective motion (Vicsek model, self-propelled particles with metric-neighbour alignment)
standard_name: Standard Vicsek model at maximal noise eta=2pi (fully disordered / random-walk limit)
citations: Vicsek, Czirok, Ben-Jacob, Cohen, Shochet 1995, Phys Rev Lett 75:1226 - original model; order-disorder kinetic transition as noise varies
Ginelli 2016, Eur Phys J Special Topics 225:2099 - review; disordered phase has residual |phi| ~ 1/sqrt(N)
arXiv 2008.09723 (Lyapunov exponent in the Vicsek model) - at eta=2pi noise is uniform iid and the dynamics equal a random walk

Vicsek model maximal noise finite-size polar order 1/sqrt(N) disordered phase

full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN, with a caveat.** The system is the standard Vicsek model. At this noise setting the literature predicts a disordered state, so the "polar order" and "local alignment" flags are most likely finite-size fluctuation or a measurement artefact, not real flocking.

**1. Model family.** This is active matter and collective motion, specifically the Vicsek model (also called the self-propelled particle model). It matches the original definition: particles are driven with a constant absolute velocity and at each time step assume the average direction of motion of the particles in their neighborhood with some random perturbation η added. Your setup has these parameters:
- Density is 400/400 = 1, with interaction radius 1, speed 0.3 and periodic boundaries.
- The noise spans the full circle, so η = 2π, the maximum.

**2. The specific behaviour.**
- **Original model.** Vicsek et al. report a kinetic phase transition from no transport (zero average velocity) to finite net transport through spontaneous symmetry breaking of the rotational symmetry. Order appears only below a critical noise η_c.
- **What happens at η = 2π.** This is the fully disordered regime. A paper on the Vicsek model's Lyapunov exponent notes that at this value the noise term is a random variable, uniform on [-π, π], drawn independently for each particle. It concludes that the Vicsek and Random Walk models present equivalent dynamics.
- **Residual order.** Ginelli's review says that in the disordered phase the headings do not cancel exactly, leading to |φ| ∼ 1/√N. For N = 400 that is about 0.05, and for N = 800 about 0.035.
- **My reasoning.** Full-circle uniform noise added to the neighbour mean erases all information about that mean. New headings are then independent and uniform, which leaves no real local alignment either.
- **Implication.** "Polar order" and "local alignment" at this setting should be consistent with a null (shuffled or random-heading) baseline. If a_polar = 6.0 and a_local_align = 5.0 are z-scores or ratios against such a baseline, check whether the baseline was computed correctly. The 800-agent variant should show a smaller residual order, about 0.035 compared with about 0.05, if the effect is only finite-size.
- **Caveat on my reading.** I assumed your "noise spanning the full circle" means the Vicsek η = 2π. If the noise were instead ±2π around the mean in a different convention, the conclusion would be the same, because that is still a fully random heading.

**3. Citations, checked against search results.**
- **Earliest source.** Vicsek, Czirók, Ben-Jacob, Cohen, Shochet (1995), "Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles", Phys. Rev. Lett. 75(6):1226–1229 (1995 Aug 7;75(6):1226-1229).
- **Review.** Ginelli (2016), "The Physics of the Vicsek Model", Eur. Phys. J. Special Topics 225, 2099–2117. It covers the algorithm, the universality class and the 1/√N disordered-phase order.
- **Supporting.** The Lyapunov-exponent paper (arXiv 2008.09723) establishes the η = 2π random-walk equivalence. I did not confirm its authors or venue from the search snippet.

I did not verify the authors, year or venue of other Vicsek-model works (for example Grégoire & Chaté 2004 on the first-order transition) from search results, so I don't cite them.

**4. Confidence: medium.** The model identification and the η = 2π disordered-phase result are well supported. Confidence is not higher because I don't know how "a_polar" and "a_local_align" are defined or normalised, so I can't say whether the 6.0 and 5.0 are a real effect, a finite-size effect or a baseline artefact.

- Ginelli The physics of the Vicsek model review 2016
